title_en: Be a breakfast eater.
title_es: Coma desayuno todos los días.
secret_en: Skipping breakfast leads to an empty feeling and a temptation to stuff yourself with unhealthy foods later in the day. And, try to eat breakfast at the table. You and your family will fill up better if you eat at the table, not while standing up or on-the-go.
secret_es: El no comer desayuno lo conduce a experimentar un sentimiento de vació, así como la tentación de comer y llenarnse de alimentos nada saludables durante el transcurso del día. Así mismo, trate de comer el desayuno sentado a la mesa. Usted y su familia se llenarán de mejor manera si ustedes comen en la mesa y no mientras están de pie, o caminando de un lado a otro.
whyItWorks_en:
Breakfast is the most important meal of the day because it will help your family’s energy level and performance in school and at work. Researchers have shown that without breakfast, you and your family are more likely to eat unhealthy foods later in the day. 

People who eat breakfast have better moods the rest of the day. Breakfast-eaters are at lower risk for heart disease and diabetes.

In addition, researchers have also discovered that you eat more slowly, digest more easily, and fill up faster if you eat meals sitting at the table. People who eat standing up, in the car, or in a hurried way tend to overeat and think less about their food choices

title_en: Be a smart server.
title_es: Sea un servidor listo.
secret_en: Use smaller bowls to limit sugary breakfast cereal. Your eyes will trick you: You and your family will actually eat less if your plates and bowls are smaller. And, you’ll still feel satisfied.
secret_es: Use tazones más chicos para limitar las cantidades de cereales de desayuno que contienen mucha azúcar. Sus ojos lo engañarán: Usted y su familia actualmente comerán menos si sus platos y tazones son chicos, además, ustedes aún así se sentirán satisfechos.
whyItWorks_en:
Researchers have studied how plate and bowl sizes affect us. We eat more when a food is served on a large dish, and less when food is served on a smaller one.

This is because a food serving appears to be larger, and therefore more satisfying, when placed on a small plate.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Be a breakfast planner.
title_es: Sea un planificador de desayunos.
secret_en: Talk about weekly breakfast items with your family, write up a list, and have everyone sign it.
secret_es: Hable con su familia acerca de las opciones semanales del desayuno, escriba una lista, y haga que todos la firmen.
whyItWorks_en: Your family will be more likely to stick to your breakfast plan if you discuss and write your commitments on a form and put them out for everyone to see. You can record what happens each day.

title_en: After breakfast, put sugary cereals far away.
title_es: Después del desayuno, guarde las cajas de cereal fuera de alcance.
secret_en: Keep them in a hard-to-reach cabinet. Out of sight really is out of mind when you feel the urge to snack.
secret_es: Mantenga las cajas de cereal en una alacena no muy accesible. "Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente" los ayudará cuando le de la ansiedad de comer algo en ayunas.
whyItWorks_en: Studies show that all of us are more likely to eat the first food we see than any other food.

title_en: Set the breakfast table the night before.
title_es: Ponga la mesa la noche anterior.
secret_en:
Prepare as much of your healthy food the night before, if possible.

If you can, use placemats or a tablecloth. Paper or cloth are both great. Put something pretty in the middle of the table, such as a plant, flower or other decoration.
secret_es:
Si es posible, prepare tanto como pueda de sus alimentos saludables, la noche anterior. 

Si usted puede, use mantelillos o un mantel. De papel o tela, ambas opciones son excelentes. Ponga algo agradable en el centro de la mesa, como una planta, flor o cualquier otra decoración.
whyItWorks_en: Did you know that the setting affects what we eat? When your family comes to the table, they’ll see that the meal is planned. This lowers stress and encourages slower eating. Family members will digest breakfast better. These steps help everyone keep a healthier weight.

title_en: Place boxes of cereal or other food containers away from the table and out of reach.
title_es: Coloque cajas de cereal u otros recipientes de comida lejos de la mesa y fuera de su alcance.
secret_en: Your family is less likely to overeat if the containers are away from the table.
secret_es: Es menos probable que su familia coma en exceso si los recipientes se encuentran alejados de la mesa.
whyItWorks_en: When taking food directly from packages or containers, people tend to overload their plates or bowls. But smaller portions can fill us up as much as larger portions. So, no eating from the box. Serve up portions in the kitchen and bring them to the table.

title_en: Measure food into one-serving portion sizes.
title_es: Mida los alimentos en raciones de una porción.
secret_en: You might be surprised at what one serving actually is! Look at the label on the package. Try measuring out cereal into one-serving portions and put each one into a baggie. Then you and your family will know how much you are really eating.
secret_es: ¡Usted podría sorprenderse del tamaño actual de lo que es una porción! Lea la etiqueta del paquete para saber cuanto es una porción. Trate de medir el cereal en cantidades de una-porción y póngalas en bolsitas de plástico. Así usted y su familia sabrán en realidad cuanto están comiendo.
whyItWorks_en: “My kids used to pour their cereal into their bowls without stopping! So, I figured out that I should put one serving size of cereal into a baggie. What a surprise when my kids saw what one serving really was! Now the kids have learned to eat just one baggie of cereal each morning. If we have fruit in the house, they add that.” Ebony, Inglewood, CA

title_en: Choose breakfast cereals carefully.
title_es: Escoja los cereales de desayuno cuidadosamente.
secret_en: Many cereals are really cookies in disguise! You can really tell what’s healthy by looking at the ingredients label. Three things to look for under “serving”: (1) 150 calories or less, (2) less than 8 grams of sugar, (3) at least 3 grams of fiber.
secret_es: ¡Muchos cereales son realmente galletas disfrazadas! Usted puede darse cuenta de lo que es saludable solo con ver los ingredientes en la etiqueta. Tres cosas a las que hay que poner atención bajo la designación de "porción" ("serving") son: (1) 150 calorías o menos, (2) menos de 8 gramos de azúcar, (3) por lo menos 3 gramos de fibra.
whyItWorks_en:
Look for “Nutrition Facts” (on the back or side). The best cereals are those where the first and second ingredients are whole grain—such as whole grain wheat or whole grain oats. 

The time you spend reading serving sizes and ingredients on packages pays off in a healthier family.

Studies show that kids will eat cereals that have less sugar if you offer them. Low-sugar cereals help your child do better during the day.

Try adding dried fruit (like raisins), fresh fruit, or nuts, if you can. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get links to other websites.

title_en: A little fat at breakfast is good.
title_es: Un poco de grasa en el desayuno es bueno.
secret_en: Peanut butter is healthy for kids and they love it. Try spreading it on toast, on top of oatmeal, or blended with banana in a smoothie.
secret_es: La mantequilla de cacahuate es saludable para los niños y a ellos les gusta. Déselas untándola en un pan tostado, poniéndosela a la avena, o mezclada con un plátano en un licuado.
whyItWorks_en: Mash an avocado and spread it on toast, instead of butter. Munch a handful of nuts, like almonds. These breakfast items will keep you and your kids feeling full the rest of the morning. And, it will help manage your blood sugar the rest of the morning.

title_en: Introduce new foods.
title_es: Introduzca alimentos nuevos.
secret_en: Do it on a weekend when everyone’s relaxed and you can try the foods with your kids.
secret_es: Hágalo durante un fin de semana cuando todos están más relajados y usted puede experimentar con esos alimentos junto con sus hijos.
whyItWorks_en:
According to research, your family will be more open to trying new foods when they aren’t stressed and when you are feeling more patient. Weekend breakfasts are a good time to get creative.

Try putting new flavors and vegetables in scrambled eggs or in smoothies. Kids are more likely to accept a new food if it’s pureed or blended.

title_en: Eat the same breakfast as your kids.
title_es: Coma el mismo desayuno que sus niños.
secret_en: They’re more likely to eat healthy breakfast foods if you eat them too. So, prepare one meal and everyone will eat healthy.
secret_es: Sus niños estarán más propensos a comer desayunos saludables si usted los come también. Prepare solo un tipo desayuno para que así todos coman saludablemente.
whyItWorks_en: Studies show that kids usually follow what their parents eat. It might take several tries, but stick with it.

title_en: Feel more full with whole grains.
title_es: Siéntase mas lleno con granos enteros ("whole grains").
secret_en:
If you serve 100% whole grain cereal or toast, your family will feel more full. This means less snacking later.

Look on package labels for “100% whole grains” or “100% whole wheat.”
secret_es:
Si usted sirve cereales o pan tostado de 100% de granos enteros, su familia se sentirá más llena. Esto significará que comerán menos bocadillos entre comidas más tarde.

Busque en las etiquetas de los paquetes que digan “100% granos enteros (whole grains)” o “100% trigo entero (whole wheat).”
whyItWorks_en:
Scientific studies show that foods with 100% whole grains are absorbed by the body more slowly than foods made from enriched or bleached flour. You’ll feel full longer. And, whole grains keep body sugars and insulin at healthy levels.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Prepare weekend breakfasts with your kids.
title_es: Prepare los desayunos del fin de semana con sus niños.
secret_en:
If your kids help make the meal, they’re more likely to eat it. Weekends are a good time to invite kids to develop cooking skills and food interests. 

Being able to cook is a great life skill. And who knows? Your child could grow up to be the next “Top Chef” or featured on the Food Network.
secret_es:
Si sus niños ayudan a preparar la comida, con mayor probabilidad la comerán. Los fines de semana ofrecen una buena oportunidad para invitar a los niños a desarrollar aptitudes para cocinar y fomentar un interés por la comida. 

El saber cocinar es una gran aptitud para toda la vida. ¿Y quien sabe?, su hijo(a) pudiera llegar a ser el próximo "Top Chef" o ser un cocinero(a) destacado(a) en la cadena de televisión "Food Network".
whyItWorks_en:
Breakfast dishes are simple for kids to help make. 

Weekend breakfasts provide time for you to be patient with the food mistakes and messes that kids may create!

If you KEEP this secret, you will get links to other websites.

title_en: Talk about food, where it comes from, and how it tastes.
title_es: Hable acerca de la comida, de donde viene, y a que sabe.
secret_en: It will help your family try new flavors. Weekend breakfasts are a good time to do this.
secret_es: Esto ayudara a su familia aprobar sabores nuevos. Los desayunos los fines de semana presentan una buena oportunidad de hacer esto.
whyItWorks_en: Talking about your healthy food will help your family to experiment with new flavors. On weekends, try talking with your kids about the different vegetables that could be added to their scrambled eggs, or how different fruit smoothies taste.

title_en: Smoothies are a healthy breakfast treat.
title_es: Los batidos de fruta y yogur son un desayuno saludable.
secret_en: VeggieBooks have lots of smoothie recipes. To get a recipe, just check that you want recipes that use a blender.
secret_es: VeggieBook tiene muchas recetas para batidos/licuados. Para obtener estas recetas, solo indique que usted desea recetas que usen una licuadora.
whyItWorks_en: Smoothies can include lots of types of fruits and vegetables. And kids are more likely to accept a new food if it’s pureed or blended. “I had never made a smoothie for myself or my family. But, I tried the smoothie recipe in my VeggieBook…and what a surprise. My husband and kids really liked it. My son told me that his favorite basketball star drinks smoothies.” Maria, Anaheim, CA

title_en: Set the mood.
title_es: Cree el ambiente propicio.
secret_en: At meals, turn off the TV, put mobile phones in another room, and say that videogames and earbuds are off limits.
secret_es: Durante las comidas, apague la televisión, ponga los teléfonos móviles en otra habitación, y diga que los juegos de video y audífonos también están prohibidos durante las comidas.
whyItWorks_en:
These devices are great in their place. But at mealtimes they’re distracting. Distracted eaters end up overeating and making poor food choices. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Making kids clean their plates can lead to overeating.
title_es: Obligar a los niños a que "se acaben todo" lo que se les sirvió, puede llevarlos a comer de más.
secret_en: Let kids respond to their body’s signals that they’re full. Let them leave some food uneaten if they want.
secret_es: Deje que los niños respondan a las señales de su cuerpo cuando están llenos. Permítales que dejen algo de lo que les sirvio sin comerselo si así lo desean.
whyItWorks_en:
Studies show that telling kids to “clean your plate” leads to overeating. The more food in front of us, the more we eat. Give your kids permission to leave some food on the plate. They’ll stop eating when their bodies tell them they’re full.

We often eat more than we need. The best way to not overeat? Keep mealtimes relaxed with plenty of time for family conversation. And encourage everyone to chew thoroughly before swallowing.

title_en: Be patient in introducing new foods--and keep trying!
title_es: ¡Sea paciente al introducir nuevos alimentos---y siga insistiendo!
secret_en: Kids usually learn to like new foods. But it will take time and patience. You may have to offer the new food many times.
secret_es: Los niños usualmente aprenden a apetecer los alimentos/platillos nuevos. Pero esto tomará tiempo y paciencia. Es probable que usted tenga que ofrecerles los alimentos nuevos varias veces.
whyItWorks_en: Guess how long it can take before we like a new food? Researchers say 8 times, on average. Introducing new foods takes patience and a low stress environment. Weekend breakfasts are a good time to try. Introducing new foods can take even longer when kids are trying to assert their independence. The best moment? When you have time to eat a relaxed meal. “I came up with three ways to deal with foods that my kids rejected. First, I said, 'You don’t have to eat it, BUT, you do have to try it.' Second, if my kids refuse the food, I take it away…BUT, I do not substitute with anything else. And, third, I serve small portions…what I call tryout-sizes! These tips take patience and persistence, but they really work.” Aisha, Oakland, CA

title_en: Eggs can be simple and quick to prepare.
title_es: Los huevos pueden ser simples y rápidos de preparar.
secret_en: Try cooking vegetables the night before and adding them to your scrambled eggs in the morning.
secret_es: Intente cocinar unas verduras la noche anterior y añádaselas a sus huevos revueltos en la mañana.
whyItWorks_en:
Eggs in the morning are healthy and easy—though best without the bacon, sausage, or other fatty meats. Eggs also reduce a craving for later snacks, so they keep you full.

Scrambled eggs are easy, and you can add vegetables to them. You could use last night’s veggie leftovers. Or just fry up some vegetables the night before to be ready. In the morning, beat eggs with a fork, put them in a pan with a bit of oil or butter, then add the vegetables. In just 5 minutes, you have a delicious, healthy breakfast. You can also add some shredded cheese.

Or, for a Mexican twist, try serving fried eggs, salsa, and cheese on top of a heated tortilla. If you want, add refried beans or extra cooked onions, garlic, tomatoes, or peppers.

title_en: Leave notes to your kids inside their packed lunches.
title_es: Déjele notitas a sus niños en sus almuerzos
secret_en: Try a message that says: “New item. Thumbs Up/Down?” Kids love to give feedback, and asking their opinion actually helps them accept new foods.
secret_es: Intente escribiendo una notita que diga: "Algo nuevo. ¿Bueno o Malo?" A los niños les encanta dar su opinión, y pidiéndoles su opinión, actualmente los ayuda a aceptar alimentos nuevos.
whyItWorks_en: Just a note that says “Hi, I’m thinking of you,” or “Good luck on your math quiz” makes packed lunches seem more special. “I even found some cute stickers to paste onto fruits and other good foods. It makes the food even more appealing.” Mai, Alhambra, CA Sometimes kids shrug off messages like these, wanting to appear strong and independent. But most of the time they notice and care.

title_en: Pack lunches for the family the night before.
title_es: Prepare los almuerzos para la familia la noche anterior.
secret_en: Measuring smaller portions will help your family not over eat.
secret_es: Midiendo las porciones ayudaran a su familia a no comer de más.
whyItWorks_en:
We are more careful at packing healthy lunches when we do it the night before, instead of during the morning rush. And packing smaller portions is important because they can fill us up just as much as big ones. Large portions can make us eat more than we need.

And, this is a great activity to do with your child.

title_en: Eat colorful, sliced vegetables and fruits.
title_es: Coma rebanadas de verduras y frutas coloridas.
secret_en: If the lunchbox is full of colorful food, we are more likely to eat it. Ask your kids to pick the colors!
secret_es: Si la "lonchera" esta llena de comida colorida, somos mas propensos a comerla. ¡Pídales a sus niños a que escojan los colores!
whyItWorks_en:
Studies show that we eat more when servings are colorful. That’s good news if you want your kids or other family members to eat more fruits and vegetables. So, for example, mix carrots with celery. And remember to cut items into bite-sized pieces. 

Some kids like Chile Piquin (also known as Pico de Gallo seasoning) on fruits and vegetables for an extra boost of flavor.

title_en: Feel more full with whole grains.
title_es: Siéntase mas llena con granos enteros ("whole grains").
secret_en: If you pack a sandwich on “100% whole grain" or "100% whole wheat” bread, your family will feel more full—which means less snacking later.
secret_es: Si usted les prepara un sándwich/emparedado con pan que sea "100% de granos enteros" ("whole grains") o "100% de trigo entero" ("whole wheat"), su familia se sentirá mas llena—lo que significa que comerán menos bocadillos/golosinas entre comidas más tarde.
whyItWorks_en:
Foods with 100% whole grains are absorbed by the body more slowly than foods made from enriched or bleached flour. That’s good because (1) whole grains will keep your family full longer, so you’ll eat less; and (2) whole grains keep glucose and insulin at healthy levels. 

Check labels for these exact words: “100% whole grain" or "100% whole wheat.”

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Try to vary what you pack for lunch each day.
title_es: Trate de variar lo que prepara de almuerzo día con día.
secret_en: Your family will be more likely to eat their healthy lunch if they aren’t bored with the same foods.
secret_es: Su familia será más propensa a comer un almuerzo saludable si no los aburre dándoles lo mismo todo los días.
whyItWorks_en: Common sense as well as research tells us that kids and adults get tired of eating the same foods. Vary the color, taste, and texture. Some days, use pita pockets instead of sliced bread. Or try hummus as a spread, rather than butter, margarine or mayonnaise. Raisins and nuts add variety. And, sliced cheese with sliced vegetables or fruit make a great combination.

title_en: Be a selective eater.
title_es: No coma de todo y escoja lo que come.
secret_en: Try to limit buffets and all-you-can-eat lunch restaurants. In these places we all tend to eat more than we need.
secret_es: Trate de limitar los "buffets" y los restaurantes que ofrecen almuerzos que le permiten servirse y comer todo lo que quiera por un precio. En estos lugares todos tendemos a comer de más
whyItWorks_en:
Research has proven that we eat more at buffets and all-you-can-eat restaurants--because we can! If you do eat at a buffet line, first, review all the food on the buffet, start to finish. Then, use a smaller plate to go through the line and choose only what you want the most and what will make you feel full.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Sip smartly.
title_es: Consuma bebidas de manera inteligente.
secret_en: Substitute water, non-fat milk, or smoothies for sugary drinks.
secret_es: Substituya agua, leche sin grasas, o batidos/licuados ("smoothies") en lugar de bebidas azucaradas.
whyItWorks_en:
Check the labels for sugar. Sports drinks, energy drinks, and fruit drinks may sound healthy, but they often have lots of sugar. Remember, 4 grams of sugar equals one small spoon. Most kids should stay under 15 grams of sugar per day, from all their eating and drinking combined. That’s less than 4 small spoons!

Adult women should keep below 25 grams, around 6 small spoons. Adult men below 37 grams, or about 9 small spoons.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Celebrate your family’s eating successes.
title_es: Festeje los éxitos alimenticios de su familia.
secret_en: Celebration calls attention to the goals you want to reach.
secret_es: Celebraciones ponen un énfasis en las metas que queremos alcanzar.
whyItWorks_en: When your family sticks to your meal commitments, think about celebrating together. Watch a family movie. Make fruit smoothies and serve them with fun straws. Put a poster on the wall and sign congratulatory messages to each other.

title_en: When at restaurants, beware of combination plates—like meals that come with a side dish and a soda.
title_es: Cuando coma en restaurantes, tenga cuidado con los platillos designados de "combinación"—como esos que vienen con algo extra e incluyen un refresco.
secret_en: Would you have bought all that separately? You can probably save money (and eat more lightly) by selecting only the items you want.
secret_es: ¿Hubiera usted comprado todo eso por separado? Usted probablemente se puede ahorrar dinero (y comer menos) al seleccionar solamente las cosas que usted quiera.
whyItWorks_en: Combination plates that come with extras, such as chips or sodas, increase the calories you get. That’s worse for your health.

title_en: Be a smart eater in restaurants.
title_es: Sea un consumidor listo en los restaurantes.
secret_en: Studies show that most people want restaurants to provide calorie labeling on their menus, though not all places do this. But, look for these clues, so that you avoid overeating.
secret_es: Estudios muestran que la mayoría de la gente quieren que restaurantes proveen listas de calorías en sus menus, aunque no todos lugares hacen esto. Pero, busquen estas claves, para evitar sobre comer.
whyItWorks_en:
Some convenience or fast food outlets now post calories, as do other restaurants. This information can help you decide what servings to choose. Health experts estimate that the average needs for adult women are met by 1,600 to 2,400 calories per day, and the average needs for adult men are 2,000 to 3,000 calories per day. The low end of each range is for inactive people, and the high end is for active individuals. Children need even fewer calories.

And remember, although a restaurant may advertise itself as “healthy” or “natural,” not all its menu items may be equally healthy.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to a website.

title_en: Be smart about low fat and fat free labels.
title_es: Sea lista acerca de las etiquetas que dicen "low-fat" ("bajas en grasas") y "fat-free" ("libres de grasas").
secret_en: “Fat free” or “low fat” doesn’t necessarily mean healthy or few calories. Low fat or fat free still can have a lot of calories. This advertising label can trick us into overeating.
secret_es: "Far free" o “Low-fat” ("Bajas en Grasas" o "libre de grasas") no necesariamente significa que sea saludable o que tenga pocas calorías. Low-fat o fat free aún puede contener muchas calorías. Este truco de publicidad nos puede engañar a que comamos de más.
whyItWorks_en:
Shocking but true: People tend to eat up to 50% more of products with a low-fat label. They eat more because they feel less guilty. 

Low fat or fat free products can still have lots of calories, sometimes almost as many calories as regular versions of the same item.

A low fat or fat free label only means fewer calories from fats. Calories can come from sugars and other ingredients. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to a website.

title_en: Surprisingly, food is a poor reward or punishment because it leads to bad eating habits.
title_es: Sorpresivamente, la comida es una forma pobre de usar como recompensa o castigo, ya que esto lleva a crear malos hábitos.
secret_en: Use other treats—such as a game or a play date or more time with sports—as a reward.
secret_es: Use otras opciones como premios, tales como un juego, o dejarlos ir a jugar con un amigo(a), o poder pasar más tiempo practicado un deporte.
whyItWorks_en:
Scientists agree that food is never good as a reward or a punishment. It’s not helpful to say things like: “If you get good grades in school, then you can have some special cake,” or “No dessert if you don’t eat your vegetables.” 

Rewarding kids with unhealthy foods (like sweets or soda) can set them up for a lifetime of eating too much sugar, fat and salt. It also encourages them to eat when they’re not hungry. 

Use other rewards for good behavior. Some ideas: more time at a favorite sport, a play date or sleepover, a trip to the library, or another round of a game.

Punishing kids by making them eat certain foods (such as their vegetables) encourages them to dislike healthy foods!

title_en: Be a storyteller.
title_es: Sea un cuenta cuentos/narrador.
secret_en: Families enjoy eating meals when they’re sharing stories about themselves.
secret_es: Las familias disfrutan sus comidas cuando comparten historias o anécdotas personales.
whyItWorks_en:
Family story-telling around the table relaxes everyone and makes dinners fun and full of discovery. To build family stories, you can ask questions like these: Do you know the source of our name? Do you know how your parents met? Have you heard about what your grandparents learned from (fill in a good or bad experience)?

If you KEEP this secret, you will get links to other websites.

title_en: Involve your kids in cooking dinner, even just with little tasks.
title_es: Involucre a sus niños en la elaboración de la cena, aunque sean tareas pequeñas.
secret_en: Kids will be more likely to eat healthy food if they help make it.
secret_es: Los niños comerán alimentos saludables con mayor probabilidad si ayudaron a prepararlos.
whyItWorks_en:
Kids think “their” dishes taste better – even when it’s vegetables. When kids help make meals, they become more open to new foods and flavors.

You could start with small tasks, like tearing up lettuce for a salad or greasing a pan for the oven. Kids enjoy reading recipes and passing along the instructions to you. It can be fun to work with kids on a recipe that they can adapt to their tastes, such as pizzas, burritos, and tortillas. Or, start kids in the kitchen with recipes they love.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Take 10 minutes on the weekend to plan weekday dinners with your family.
title_es: Tómese 10 minutos con su familia el fin de semana para planificar las cenas de la semana.
secret_en: When you plan together, you’ll be more likely to eat healthy dinners all week.
secret_es: Cuando planifican juntos, ustedes serán más propensos a comer cenas saludables toda la semana.
whyItWorks_en:
If you talk with your family about the week’s healthy meals (like those in VeggieBooks), you help everyone work up an appetite for them. 

Also, planning helps you shop more carefully, saving money and not wasting food.

title_en: Let your kids make some decisions about what to have for dinner.
title_es: Deje que sus niños tomen algunas decisiones acerca de lo que se preparará para la cena.
secret_en: They’ll eat more healthy foods if they take part in choosing them.
secret_es: Los niños comerán más alimentos saludables si ellos participan en escogerlos.
whyItWorks_en:
University research and smart Moms have proven that kids are more likely to eat healthy food when they’ve chosen it themselves. Instead of pressuring them to eat a particular food, offer them a choice of two healthy meals: “Would you like this dish using carrots or this dish using broccoli?” Kids like helping make the decision, and they end up eating well in either case. 

Here’s another Mom-tested idea. When introducing a new food, have kids taste a bit using their hands (after washing!). Even with soup, have them dip a finger and lick it clean. People tend to like the taste of foods sampled in this ancient way.

title_en: Serve dinner on smaller plates, if you have them.
title_es: Sirva la cena en platos chicos, si los tiene.
secret_en: Rule of thumb: We tend to eat less when the food is on smaller plates.
secret_es: Regla general: Nosotros tendemos a comer menos cuando la comida es servida en platos chicos.
whyItWorks_en:
Studies show that smaller portions fill us up as much as larger portions. 

The larger the plate or bowl, the more people eat, sometimes simply because the food is there. But that’s often more than we really need.

On a smaller plate, a smaller portion size still looks good, and usually it’s sufficient.

title_en: Serve salads or a soup first at dinner.
title_es: A la hora de la cenar, sirva ensaladas o sopas primero.
secret_en: By serving a salad or a soup first, you and your family will fill up on healthy food.
secret_es: Al servirse una ensalada o una sopa primero, usted y su familia se llenarán con alimentos saludables.
whyItWorks_en: When you start a meal with healthy food, then you can serve smaller portions of more calorie-rich dishes. You’ll all feel fuller on less food.

title_en: Surprisingly, food is a poor reward or punishment because it leads to bad eating habits.
title_es: Sorpresivamente, la comida es una forma pobre e inútil de usar como recompensa o castigo, ya que esto lleva a crear malos hábitos.
secret_en: Use other treats—such as a game or a play date or more time with sports—as a reward.
secret_es: Utilice otras formas para premiar a sus niños—como el poder jugar más, ir a la casa de un amigo(a), o practicar deportes por más tiempo.
whyItWorks_en:
Studies agree that food is never a good bribe. Kids eat better when food isn’t linked to emotions or a feeling of being good (rewarded) or bad (punished). If you try to control what your kids eat by denying, rewarding, pressuring, or punishing them, you’ll have the opposite effect. They’ll want the forbidden foods even more and will dislike the foods that you want them to try.

Also, while it’s tempting to give sweets when your child feels sad or as a special treat, that teaches a lesson that isn’t healthy in the long run. It tells your child that it’s okay to eat when he or she isn’t hungry. That can cause unhealthy weight gain.

title_en: Make the same dinner for adults and kids.
title_es: Prepare la misma cena para adultos y niños
secret_en: Your kids are more likely to eat healthy dinners if your entire family eats the same food.
secret_es: Sus niños son mas propensos a comer cenas saludables si toda la familia come lo mismo.
whyItWorks_en: When children watch adults trying new foods and flavors, they’re more likely to do it themselves. Be patient. This may take several attempts. Carolina from East Los Angeles tells her story: “My son was a picky eater so I used to make two dinners--one for me and my husband and one for my son. Then I tried planning dinners with my son, trying to recognize his opinion about some dishes. Now, I make one healthy dinner and everyone gets something they like.” If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Gather all the family to eat dinner together at the table.
title_es: Reúna a toda la familia a comer la cena juntos en la mesa.
secret_en: You’ll all eat more slowly and make better choices if you’re together at the table. No dinners while standing or on-the-go. No kids eating in their rooms, away from the rest of family.
secret_es: Todos ustedes comerán de manera más lenta y tomarán mejores decisiones si están todos juntos en la mesa. No coma de pie o a la carrera. No permita que sus niños coman en sus cuartos, alejados del resto de la familia.
whyItWorks_en:
Nutrition studies show that when we eat sitting at the table, we eat more slowly and digest more easily. The opposite is true when we eat standing up, in the car, or in a hurried way: That’s when we over eat. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Ask friends what healthy dinners work for their families.
title_es: Pregúntele a sus amistades que cenas saludables les gustan a sus familias.
secret_en: All of us are more likely to try a new dish if friends like it.
secret_es: Todos nosotros somos más propensos a querer probar un platillo nuevo si este les gusto a nuestros amigos.
whyItWorks_en:
Sometimes a kid doesn’t like a certain vegetable dish just because it’s unknown. Ask some other Moms: “What healthy meals work well in your home?” Point out to your kid that his or her friend likes that meal.

You also could join forces with other Moms. Together, you can decide on healthy dishes to try. VeggieBooks give you plenty of recipe ideas.

title_en: Try to vary how you fix food.
title_es: Trate de variar como prepara la comida.
secret_en: Mix it up! Your family will like a healthy dinner more if they aren’t bored with it.
secret_es: ¡Varíelas! A su familia le gustara más una cena saludable si no se han aburrido de ella.
whyItWorks_en: We all get bored eating a food prepared the same way again and again. For example, shredding carrots in a salad is great, but people get tired of carrots if that’s the only way they see them. Try roasting carrots with other vegetables, or do a stir-fry. It’s easier than it sounds. “I have tried lots of the VeggieBook recipes. I was so happy to see my family enjoy the broccoli burritos—we had never tried anything like that before. And, their favorite dish was Sloppy Joes. My family was shocked to discover that it had cabbage in it. I can’t wait to work my way through more of the recipes.” Gloria, San Luis Obispo VeggieBooks have nearly 300 simple but delicious recipes covering 10 different vegetables.

title_en: Be a dinner planner and create a good mood.
title_es: Sea un planificador de cenas y cree un buen ambiente.
secret_en:
Set dinner places for everyone at a table. Create a calm atmosphere; try paper or cloth placemats or tablecloth. 

If possible, put something pretty in the middle, such as a plant, flower, candle, or other decoration.
secret_es:
Asegúrese que todos tengan un lugar en la mesa. Cree un ambiente de tranquilidad; trate de usar mantelillos de papel o tela o un mantel. 

Si es posible, coloque algo bonito en el centro de la mesa, como una planta, flor, vela u otro adorno.
whyItWorks_en:
Did you know that mood (the “vibe”) affects how we eat? Scientists found that people eat more slowly and feel fuller when the table is set and lights have been lowered. Loud music and bright lighting create a hectic atmosphere that interferes with relaxed dining.

Also, don’t scold the kids or take up family arguments at dinner or any other meal. These negative emotions lead to overeating.

title_en: Preserve dinner-time calm by banning electronic devices during the meal.
title_es: Preserve la tranquilidad a la hora de comer prohibiendo dispositivos electrónicos durante la cena.
secret_en: While eating, turn off the TV, put mobile phones in another room, and say that videogames and ear phones are off limits.
secret_es: Mientras comen, apague la televisión, ponga los teléfonos móviles en otra habitación, y dígales a sus hijos que los juegos de video y audífonos también están prohibidos.
whyItWorks_en: All these devices are great in their place. But at mealtimes they’re distracting. Distracted eaters end up overeating and making poor food choices, like loading up on calorie-rich items and skipping salads and other veggies.

title_en: Eat smarter without weighing or measuring food.
title_es: Coma de manera más inteligente sin tener que pesar o medir la comida.
secret_en: You can create a “healthy plate” by dividing your plate into 3 sections—protein (meat or fish), grains, and vegetables. As the picture shows, meat or fish should cover about one-quarter of the plate, grains about one-quarter, and vegetables one-half.
secret_es: Usted puede crear un "plato saludable" al dividir su plato en 3 secciones—proteína (carne o pescado), granos, y verduras. Como muestra la imagen, la carne o pescado debe cubrir aproximadamente una cuarta parte del plato, granos alrededor de una cuarta parte, y las verduras una mitad.
whyItWorks_en:
Protein can include chicken, turkey, fish, or meat. Try to eat whole grains, such as brown rice, whole wheat noodles, and barley or bulgur in soups and stews. VeggieBook has lots of tasty vegetable recipes you can try. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Choose wisely at buffets and all-you-can-eat dinner restaurants.
title_es: Elija sabiamente en los "buffets" u otros restaurantes donde usted puede comer todo lo que quiere por un precio fijo.
secret_en: It’s too easy to eat more than you need.
secret_es: Es muy fácil comer más de lo que usted necesita.
whyItWorks_en:
Research has proven that we eat more at buffets and all-you-can-eat restaurants--because we can! If you do eat at a buffet line, first, review all the food on the buffet, start to finish. Then, use a smaller plate to go through the line and choose only what you want the most and what will make you feel full.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: When eating out, pay attention to portion size and eat only what you really need.
title_es: Cuando salga a comer, ponga atención al tamaño de las porciones y solo coma lo que usted realmente necesita.
secret_en: Oftentimes, restaurant portions are very large. Consider sharing one serving with a friend rather than buying two. Or take home the leftovers for another meal.
secret_es: Con frecuencia, las porciones que sirven en los restaurantes son muy grandes. Considere compartir un platillo con una amiga(o) en lugar de comprar dos. O llévese a casa lo que haya sobrado para comerlo otro día.
whyItWorks_en:
Many restaurants or fast-food chains offer giant-sized servings to look generous or make it seem like you’re getting a deal. You’ve seen it: the heaping mound of pasta, the huge steak, the foot-long sandwiches, and the large desserts. Order less, save money, and eat just as well. 

How to know how much to order? Ask waiters about portion sizes, or look at plates being served to others. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Talk about your food at dinner.
title_es: Hable acerca de su comida durante la cena.
secret_en: It will spark your family’s interest in eating new foods.
secret_es: Esto despertará el interés de su familia en comer comidas o platillos nuevos.
whyItWorks_en: Research shows that talking about where food comes from, how it tastes, and how it feels on the tongue makes us slow down and enjoy it more. Talking about food also makes us more open to new flavors.

title_en: Forget the “clean plate club.”
title_es: Olvídese del "club limpia platos".
secret_en: Forcing people to clean their plates often encourages them to overeat.
secret_es: Forzando a la gente a que se coman todo dejando el plato limpio, a menudo los incita a comer de más.
whyItWorks_en: Studies show that telling kids to “clean your plate” leads to overeating. The more food in front of us, the more we eat. Give your kids permission to leave some food on the plate. They’ll stop eating when their bodies tell them they’re full. We often eat more than we need. The best way to not overeat? Keep mealtimes relaxed with plenty of time for family conversation. And encourage everyone to chew thoroughly before swallowing.

title_en: Slow it down.
title_es: Baje el ritmo cuando coma.
secret_en: Our bodies naturally feel full if we give them enough time to register what we’ve eaten.
secret_es: Nuestros cuerpos se sienten llenos naturalmente si les damos suficiente tiempo para registrar lo que hemos comido.
whyItWorks_en: The best way to avoid overeating? Keep mealtimes relaxed with plenty of time for family conversation. Urge kids to chew thoroughly before swallowing. Put down the fork or spoon between mouthfuls. This allows the body’s hunger signals to respond to what’s been eaten. Children are naturally slow eaters…just as they walk slower than adults. So, slow down your eating! “I was talking to our doctor about my daughter’s eating. She always rushes through her meals. The doctor suggested that I teach my daughter to count to 5 between mouthfuls of food. So, that’s what we all do now…count to 5 between bites! It has helped my daughter, my husband, and me.” Laila, Long Beach, CA

title_en: When at restaurants, beware of combination plates—like meals that come with a side dish and a soda.
title_es: Cuando coma en restaurantes, tenga cuidado con los platillos designados de "combinación"—como esos que vienen con algo extra e incluyen un refresco/soda.
secret_en: Would you have bought all that separately? You can probably save money (and eat more lightly) by selecting only the items you want.
secret_es: ¿Hubiera usted comprado todo eso por separado? Usted probablemente se puede ahorrar dinero (y comer menos al mismo tiempo) al seleccionar solamente las cosas que usted quiere.
whyItWorks_en: Combination plates that come with extras, such as chips or sodas, increase the calories you get. That’s worse for your health.

title_en: Celebrate your family’s eating successes.
title_es: Festeje los éxitos alimenticios de su familia.
secret_en: Celebration calls attention to goals you want to reach.
secret_es: Celebraciones ponen un énfasis en las metas que queremos alcanzar.
whyItWorks_en: When your family sticks to your meal commitments, think about celebrating together. Watch a family movie. Make fruit smoothies and serve them with fun straws. Put a poster on the wall and sign congratulatory messages to each other.

title_en: Teasing or embarrassing someone for being overweight just makes the situation worse.
title_es: El burlarse o hacer que alguien se avergüence por estar pasado de peso solo empeora la situación.
secret_en: People treated this way overeat even more.
secret_es: Las personas que son tratadas de esta manera tienden a comer de mas, aún más.
whyItWorks_en:
Studies show that embarrassing someone for being overweight (“Look at the shape you’re in!”) makes that person twice as likely to become even heavier. 

Teasing a person for being overweight also just makes the situation worse. It convinces the person that he or she is lazy and weak-willed. Now convinced of this, the person just gives up trying to eat carefully. 

Instead, accept others for who they are, regardless of their weight. Or, offer to help a person eat less and eat more healthily but without labeling the person as “fat” or “obese.” That way, the person can maintain self-respect and feel good being around you.

title_en: Be a smart eater in restaurants.
title_es: Sea un consumidor astuto en los restaurantes.
secret_en: Studies show that most people want restaurants to provide calorie labeling on their menus, though not all places do this. But, look for these clues, so that you avoid overeating.
secret_es: Estudios muestran que la mayoría de la gente quieren que restaurantes proveen listas de calorías en sus menus, aunque no todos lugares hacen esto. Pero, busquen estas claves, para evitar sobre comer.
whyItWorks_en:
Some convenience or fast food outlets now post calories, as do other restaurants. This information can help you decide what servings to choose. Health experts estimate that the average needs for adult women are met by 1,600 to 2,400 calories per day, and the average needs for adult men are 2,000 to 3,000 calories per day. The low end of each range is for inactive people, and the high end is for active individuals. Children need even fewer calories.

And remember, although a restaurant may advertise itself as “healthy” or “natural,” not all its menu items may be equally healthy.

title_en: Be smart about low fat and fat free labels.
title_es: Sea lista acerca de las etiquetas que dicen low-fat (bajo en grasas) y fat free (libre de grasas).
secret_en: “Fat free” or “low fat” doesn’t necessarily mean healthy or few calories. Low fat or fat free can still have a lot of calories. This advertising label can trick us into overeating.
secret_es: "Fat free" (libre de grasas) o “Low-fat” (bajo en grasas) no necesariamente significa saludable o menos calorías. Low fat o fat free aún puede contener muchas calorías. Este truco de publicidad puede engañarnos a que comamos de más.
whyItWorks_en:
Shocking but true: People tend to eat up to 50% more of products with a low fat label. They eat more because they feel less guilty. 

But low fat or fat free products can still have lots of calories, sometimes almost as many calories as regular versions of the same item.

A low fat or fat free label only means fewer calories from fats. Calories can come from sugars and other ingredients. 

If you KEEP this secret, you will get links to other websites.

title_en: Be persistent in introducing new foods.
title_es: Sea persistente en introducir comidas/alimentos nuevos.
secret_en: Sometimes we have to try a food several times before we enjoy it.
secret_es: A veces tenemos que probar una comida varias veces antes de que la disfrutemos.
whyItWorks_en: Researchers have uncovered an interesting fact about how long it takes to “learn to like” new foods. On average it takes 8 times! Introducing new foods takes patience and a low-stress atmosphere. So, weekends are often the best time to sample new tastes. The best time to try new foods? When you have time to eat at a relaxed meal. Making a soup is a good way to introduce a new vegetable. VeggieBooks have great soup recipes. “I came up with three ways to deal with foods that my kids rejected. First, I said, ‘You don’t have to eat it, BUT, you do have to try it.’ Second, if my kids refuse the food, I take it away…BUT, I do not substitute with anything else. And, third, I serve small portions…what I call tryout-sizes!” Aisha, Oakland, CA

title_en: Looking for new snack ideas?
title_es: ¿En busca de ideas nuevas para bocadillos?
secret_en:
There are lots of ways to eat healthy and feel full. Select the VeggieBook option for snacks.

You can always add snack ideas by making a new VeggieBook.
secret_es:
Hay muchas maneras de comer saludablemente y sentirse lleno. Seleccione la opción para bocadillos de VeggieBook.

Usted siempre puede añadir ideas para bocadillos al crear un VeggieBook nuevo.
whyItWorks_en:
Make your own trail mix from nuts and dried fruits. It’s much less expensive to buy the ingredients in bulk than to buy prepared mixes. Store individual servings in small plastic bags.

Another idea: Spoon peanut butter onto celery sticks or apple slices. Or, slice jicama or peppers to munch.

Studies show that eating a small snack slowly satisfies hunger just as much as eating a big snack. Sounds impossible, but it’s true!

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to a website.

title_en: Use vegetable or fruit smoothies as a snack.
title_es: Use batidos/licuados de verduras o frutas como un bocadillo.
secret_en: Pick any veggie in VeggieBook (except potatoes and onions) and ask for recipes that use a blender or food processor. You’ll find one for a smoothie.
secret_es: Escoja cualquier verdura en VeggieBook (excepto papas o cebollas) y opte por recetas que usen una licuadora o procesador de alimentos. Usted encontrará una para un batido/licuado.
whyItWorks_en:
We sip a cold smoothie more slowly than we munch through handfuls of chips. Smoothies give satisfaction without unhealthy salt, fats, and extra calories.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Slice fruits and vegetables to make them even more attractive.
title_es: Parta o rebane las frutas y verduras para hacerlas aun más atractivas.
secret_en: Try colorful sliced fruit, or vegetable slices with cheese.
secret_es: Haga la prueba con fruta de colores vivos en rebanadas, o con verduras rebanadas con queso.
whyItWorks_en:
Fruit is a great substitute for sugar. Slicing fruits, such as an apple, orange, or banana, makes them easier to eat.

Same goes for vegetables, which is why carrot sticks are a more popular snack than whole carrots. And, peanut butter on celery sticks is an easy treat.


Lots of people sprinkle Chile Piquin on fruits and vegetables for an extra boost of flavor.

Braces and missing teeth can keep kids from wanting to eat fruit or a vegetable in front of others. And kids have smaller hands. Slice a healthy snack to help them out!

title_en: Be a smart snacker.
title_es: Sea un comedor de bocadillos listo.
secret_en: Avoid eating directly from a package of snack food, even nuts or raisins. You’ll eat more than you planned and more than you need to feel full.
secret_es: Evite comer directamente del paquete o de la bolsa de un bocadillo/golosina, incluyendo nueces o pasas. Usted comerá más de lo que planeaba y más de lo que necesita para sentirse lleno.
whyItWorks_en:
When we eat snacks from a package, we lack any visual signals that we have eaten enough. So we just keep on munching, and eat way more than a serving size, or even two!

Take out what you want, use a plate or bowl, and put away the package. Then sit down at a table to snack. You’ll enjoy your food more and consume less at the same time.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to a website.

title_en: Take a few extra minutes to help your family snack smartly.
title_es: Tome unos minutos extras para ayudar a su familia a que coman "entre comidas" de manera inteligente.
secret_en: Divide packaged snacks like chips, crackers, or trail mix into bags that contain one serving each.
secret_es: Divida los bocadillos empaquetados como las papitas, galletas saladas o una mezcla de frutas secas y nueces ("trail mix") en bolsitas de plástico con la cantidad de una porción cada una.
whyItWorks_en:
Look at the Nutrition Facts on packages (on the side or back) to learn how many pieces make one serving. Then, measure out servings into separate baggies. 

How many potato chips do you need to feel full? Surprisingly, less than half of what you might think. Researchers checked out chocolate chips, apple pie and potato chips. Studies showed that smaller portions make us feel just as full as larger ones.

So, make it a rule that if family members insist on snacking on unhealthy food, they can only have a single serving.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to a website.

title_en: Place healthy snacks where they’re easy to see and grab, like the front of the refrigerator shelves.
title_es: Coloque los bocadillos saludables donde estén accesibles y al alcance, como en las repisas de enfrente del refrigerador.
secret_en: Making foods easy to reach will increase their popularity..
secret_es: Colocando los alimentos al alcance incrementará su popularidad.
whyItWorks_en: Your family will be more likely to eat well when the good stuff is within easy reach. As for the bad stuff: Out of sight helps it stay out of mind. “My family likes to snack. So I put carrot and celery sticks in the refrigerator and my kids can snack on them. A little peanut butter on celery sticks is good, too. If we have broccoli, my kids like to dip it in yogurt…they call if putting snow on the trees. And, whenever I have fresh fruit, that’s the first thing the kids go for.” Mary, Pasadena, CA Research agrees with this Mom. We all eat food that’s right in front of us more than when it’s hard to get to.

title_en: Eat 3 healthy meals a day and just one snack.
title_es: Coma 3 comidas saludables y una botana al día.
secret_en: Stick to breakfast, lunch, snack, and dinner. With just one light snack mid-afternoon, your family won’t over eat.
secret_es: Mantenga un régimen de desayuno, almuerzo, bocadillo, y cena. Con solo un bocadillo ligero en la tarde, su familia no comerá de más.
whyItWorks_en:
We all need a snack sometimes, especially kids. But you can help your family be healthy by limiting snacks to once a day. 

It’s best not to snack an hour or two before dinner or just before going to bed.

Try having healthy snacks readily available like veggies with hummus or salsa or a yogurt dip. And some cheese with sliced fruit is much better than chips.

title_en: Remind your kids to stop eating when they feel full.
title_es: Recuérdeles a sus hijos que paren de comer una vez que se sientan llenos.
secret_en: They’ll usually feel just as satisfied with a smaller portion.
secret_es: Ellos por lo general se sentirán igual de satisfechos comiendo una porción más chica.
whyItWorks_en: “My daughter was always hungry. So, I started giving her a small snack after school. That satisfied her, and now she has room for a healthy dinner.” Yolanda, El Monte, CA Help kids eat their snacks slowly. That allows their digestive system time to send a message to their brains: “I’ve had enough for now.”

title_en: Write calorie counts on the front of packages of less-healthy snack foods.
title_es: Escriba el contenido de calorías en la parte de enfrente de los paquetes de bocadillos que son menos saludables.
secret_en: It will make you and your family think twice when choosing a snack.
secret_es: Esto hará que usted y su familia lo piensen dos veces cuando vayan a escoger un bocadillo.
whyItWorks_en: “I look at a package’s Nutrition Facts to find out how many calories are in one serving. Then, I use a marker pen to write that number on the box. When I open my cabinet and see a big black ‘230’, I think again.” Rosa, Montclair, CA If you KEEP this secret, you will get a link to another website.

title_en: Be a choosy beverage drinker.
title_es: No tome de todo y sea selecto.
secret_en: Substitute water, non-fat milk, or smoothies for sugary drinks.
secret_es: Substituya agua, leche sin grasas, o batidos/licuados ("smoothies") en lugar de bebidas azucaradas.
whyItWorks_en:
Check the labels for sugar. Sports drinks, energy drinks, and fruit drinks may sound healthy, but they often have lots of sugar. Remember, 4 grams of sugar equals one small spoon. Most kids should stay under 15 grams of sugar per day, from all their eating and drinking combined. That’s less than 4 small spoons!

Adult women should keep below 25 grams, around 6 small spoons. Adult men below 37 grams, or about 9 small spoons.

title_es: Sea persistente al introducir alimentos nuevos.
secret_en: Sometimes we have to try a new food several times before we enjoy it.
secret_es: A veces tenemos que probar una comida varias veces antes de que la disfrutemos.
whyItWorks_en: Here’s an interesting fact about how long it takes to “learn” new foods: 8 tries, on average. Introducing new foods takes patience and a low-stress atmosphere. Weekends are often the best time. Remember, kids seldom learn good food choices simply because you tell them “eat this, it’s good for you.” You have to enjoy the food yourself. Next time you tell your child to try broccoli topped with yogurt or salsa, and she or he makes a face, take a bite yourself and keep trying. “I came up with three ways to deal with foods that my kids rejected. First, I said, ‘You don’t have to eat it, BUT, you do have to try it. Second, if my kids refuse the food, I take it away…BUT, I do not substitute with anything else. And, third, I serve small portions…what I call tryout-sizes!" Aisha, Oakland, CA Kids are more accepting of a food if they know something about it, so tell them a simple fact or two. For example, “carrots grow underground and have to be dug up.” Search the Internet for fun facts about vegetables and fruits.

title_en: Buy generics for the basics.
title_es: Compre marcas genéricas para los artículos básicos.
secret_en: Brand-name products often aren’t any different from generics or a grocery chain’s label. They’re just more expensive and have more attractive packaging and advertising to make you spend extra money.
secret_es: Los productos de marcas reconocidas frecuentemente no son diferentes a los productos de marcas genéricas o a los productos que llevan la marca de la tienda. Los productos de "marca" son solamente más caros, vienen en paquetes más atractivos e incluyen campañas de publicidad para hacer que usted gaste más dinero.
whyItWorks_en:
For the basics—like sugar, flour, butter, milk, and canned foods—generic products will be almost exactly the same as the advertised brands.

title_en: Be a smart shopper.
title_es: Sea un comprador informado.
secret_en: Beware of items you see at the ends of aisles or at the check-out line. Stores put items here because they make the highest profit for the store. But these items often have too much fat, sugar, or salt. Profits for the store, but not good for you!
secret_es: Tenga cuidado con los productos y artículos que se encuentran al final de los pasillos y alrededor de las cajas registradoras. Las tiendas ponen esos productos ahí por que son los que le aportan a la tienda las ganancias más altas. Pero con frecuencia estos productos contienen demasiadas grasas, azúcar o sal. ¡Ganancias para la tienda sí, pero dañinos para usted y su familia!
whyItWorks_en: “My kids always want to buy candy when we’re standing in the check-out line. They start whining and complaining and it’s always a battle. Now, I bring a baggie of fruit slices with us to the store and pull it out while we’re in line. Problem solved!” Veronica, Fillmore, CA Little-known secret: Grocery stores put the items we really need most (such as milk) in the farthest corners of the store. That means we have to pass the ends of a lot of aisles to get there. What do stores put at the ends of aisles? The items that give them the most profit, of course. Once we see things, we’re more likely to buy them. But these are often the least healthy items. Don’t fall for it!

title_en: Be a careful shopper.
title_es: Sea una compradora precavida.
secret_en: Watch out for promotions like “10 for $10.” You don’t have to buy all 10! The price is the same whether you buy 2 items or 10. You will pay $1 per item, whatever quantity you need.
secret_es: Tenga cuidado con las promociones como "10 por $10". ¡Usted no tiene por que comprar los 10 artículos! El precio es el mismo sin importar si usted compra 2 artículos o 10. Usted pagará $1 por artículo, sin importar la cantidad que necesite.
whyItWorks_en: Special combination or bulk deals encourage us to buy more than we need. Just because the offer is 5 for $3.50 doesn’t mean you need 5. Remember, the price is the same no matter how many you buy.

title_en: Stick to your shopping list.
title_es: Apéguese a su lista de compras y no compre nada que no este en la lista.
secret_en: You’ll save money and avoid unhealthy foods you don’t really need.
secret_es: Usted ahorrará dinero y evitará alimentos no saludables que realmente no necesita.
whyItWorks_en: Often, colorful packages or banners in the store pull us into buying things we don’t really need. “Gee,” we think, “that looks fun.” But these items often are not your friends. Don’t fall for the dazzle, a store’s promotions, or something you’ve seen on TV. Stick to your shopping list, and your family will eat more healthy and for less money.

title_en: Be an alert shopper.
title_es: Sea un comprador alerta.
secret_en: Look for deals on the shelves above or below eye-level. You’ll save money by looking for brands in less visible locations.
secret_es: Busque ofertas y especiales en las repisas por encima y por debajo del nivel de sus ojos. Usted ahorrará dinero al buscar y considerar marcas que se encuentran en lugares menos visibles.
whyItWorks_en: Because we’re more likely to buy the first thing we see, supermarkets put the items where they make the most money right at your eye level. Look above and below for brands on other shelves. These items may be less promoted, but they are often just as good and often cost less.

title_en: Question the product claims on the front of packages.
title_es: Cuestione las afirmaciones de los productos hechas en la parte frontal de los paquetes.
secret_en: “Fat free” or “low fat” doesn’t necessarily mean healthy or few calories. Low fat or fat free can still have a lot of calories. This advertising label can trick us into overeating.
secret_es: "Far free" o “Low-fat” ("Bajas en Grasas" o "libre de grasas") no necesariamente significa que sea saludable o de pocas calorías. Low-fat o fat free aún puede contener muchas calorías. Este truco de publicidad nos puede engañar a que comamos de más.
whyItWorks_en:
Beware of product claims on the front of packages. But, you can trust the "Nutrition Facts" on the side or back of packages. These "Facts" must follow strict government rules.

Seeing a low-fat or fat free label can encourage us to overeat. Shocking but true: People tend to eat up to 50% more of products with a low fat label. They eat more because they feel less guilty. 

A low fat or fat free label only means fewer calories from fats. Calories can come from sugars and other ingredients.

title_en: Be a thoughtful shopper.
title_es: Sea un comprador inteligente.
secret_en: Think twice before buying items on sale or marked “good while supplies last.” That’s the advertising talking. Ask yourself if you really need it.
secret_es: Piense dos veces antes de comprar artículos "en oferta" o que han sido marcados como "mientras duren las existencias". Estas frases son pura publicidad. Pregúntese si realmente los necesita.
whyItWorks_en: “Whenever I see a food on sale, I want to buy it. It’s natural to want to grab a good deal. But I’ve learned better. Now I ask myself two questions: Do we really need it, right now? And, is it really cheaper than normal? If I answer no to either question, I don’t buy it.” Debbie, Northridge, CA Often stores will promote a product “on sale” or “while supplies last” just to make us think that it’s about to become scarce. But, in fact, the product is usually available at pretty much the same price. Don’t buy just because something’s on sale. Ask if it’s what you and your family really need, right now, for a healthy lifestyle.

title_en: Be a smart food planner when you shop.
title_es: Sea un planificador de alimentos preparado cuando vaya de compras.
secret_en: A famous food writer shares his great “Food Rules.” Your family can learn some important facts about healthy eating.
secret_es: Un escritor de comida famoso comparte sus grandes "Reglas de Alimentos". Su familia podría aprender algunos hechos importantes acerca de la alimentación saludable.
whyItWorks_en:
Michael Pollan helps you discover the healthiest foods to look for when shopping.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a weblink to his Food Rules, plus lots of other tips.

title_en: Many drinks are loaded with sugar.
title_es: Muchas bebidas están cargadas de azúcar
secret_en: Lots of drinks have much more sugar than you would expect. These drinks are not the healthiest for your family. Try to avoid them when shopping.
secret_es: Muchas bebidas contienen mucho más azúcar de lo que usted se imagina. Estas bebidas no son las más saludables para su familia. Trate de evitarlas cuando vaya de compras.
whyItWorks_en: If you KEEP this secret, you will get a weblink to an online “sugar calculator.” This shows how much sugar you drink, without knowing it, from different kinds of drinks.

title_en: Dietary guidelines and other food facts can help you shop smarter.
title_es: Normas dietéticas y otros datos/hechos de alimentos pueden ayudarla a tomar buenas decisiones cuando va de compras.
secret_en: There are lots of interesting and important facts that you and your family can learn about food. These will help guide your family to the healthiest meals.
secret_es: Hay muchos datos interesantes e importantes que usted y su familia pueden aprender acerca de los alimentos. Estos datos ayudarán a guiar a su familia hacia las comidas más saludables.
whyItWorks_en:
Important food facts from healthcare professionals have been gathered in one place.

If you KEEP this secret, you will get a web link to the Consumer Corner at the Food and Nutrition Information Center.
